description: Replace the random forest with a LightGBM binary classifier on concatenated Morgan count fingerprints (2048 bits, radius 2) and all RDKit 2D descriptors, using the specified hyperparameters.

Replace the single LightGBM fit with an average of 5 LightGBM models, each seeded seed*10+i with bagging fraction 0.7 (subsample=0.7, subsample_freq=1), computing features once and averaging predicted probabilities.

Abort the BBB rule-prior feature idea: the current LightGBM script already computes TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors and the acid-group counts (fr_COO, fr_tetrazole) through RDKit Descriptors.descList, so the proposed rule-score features would be near-duplicates the trees can already split on.

Standardize each molecule before featurization by keeping its heaviest fragment, neutralizing charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, and falling back to the parsed original if standardization fails.

Replace the single LightGBM predictor with an equal-weight rank average of three models (RandomForest on Morgan count bits, LightGBM on bits plus descriptors, and logistic regression on standardized descriptors), so the predictions are combined by rank rather than by probability.

Swap the LightGBM classifier for a CatBoostClassifier (600 iterations, learning rate 0.05, depth 6, l2_leaf_reg 3, seeded by the seed argument) on the existing Morgan-count plus RDKit-descriptor features.
Abort the Tanimoto-kernel SVM idea: it is a model-family swap, which the experiment notes say to avoid, and it would replace the current LightGBM predictor that is the only clear win so far.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement: the diff only swaps the Morgan fingerprint generator for an atom-pair count fingerprint with the same N_BITS. It adds no file access, pasted answers or use of test labels.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. Atom-pair count fingerprints are a valid featurization, and the featurize call and output shape stay the same. Minor point: RADIUS is no longer used by featurize and could be removed to keep the code simple.

The gain of 0.0031 in loss is smaller than the single-run noise (sd 0.0049), so rejecting on one run is consistent with the numbers. If slots allow, a replicate might be worth it, because the change is a one-line edit with no extra code.

description: Swap the Morgan count fingerprint for a 2048-bit atom-pair count fingerprint, keeping the LightGBM model and RDKit descriptors, to test whether atom-pair topology adds signal beyond circular fingerprints.

Replace the single LightGBM predictor with a stacked ensemble: inner 5-fold out-of-fold predictions from LightGBM and RandomForest feed a LogisticRegression meta-model, while test predictions come from both base models refit on all training data.
Add a Laplacian-corrected naive Bayes predictor over binary ECFP4 bits and rank-average its sigmoid score with the existing LightGBM probability at equal weight.

Replace the single radius-2 2048-bit Morgan count fingerprint with concatenated radius 1, 2 and 3 Morgan count fingerprints of 1024 bits each (3072 bits total), keeping the current LightGBM model and the RDKit descriptors; the spec's RandomForest is not used because the incumbent is already LightGBM.
Abort: the idea is already implemented, since featurize() in the current train.py already uses GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy with the radius-2, 2048-bit Morgan generator.

Build the Morgan count fingerprint with RDKit's feature-invariant (FCFP-style) atom invariants, radius 2 and 2048 bits, leaving the LightGBM model and descriptors unchanged. The spec's "keep the RandomForest" refers to the old model; the incumbent is LightGBM, so that is what stays.

Abort the ExtraTrees idea: the spec targets RandomForestClassifier, which is no longer in train.py (slot 0 already replaced it with LightGBM), so this would be a model-family swap from LightGBM, which the notes say to avoid.

Train LightGBM at learning rate 0.02 with up to 2000 rounds, choose the round count by early stopping (100) on a seeded stratified 15% split of the training fold, then refit on the full fold with 1.1 times the best iteration.
Aborted the XGBoost idea: it swaps only the library for the same gradient-boosted-tree family as the incumbent LightGBM, and its spec drops the RDKit descriptors that the current model uses.
Drop constant feature columns (computed on training rows only and applied to test rows), then train LightGBM with extra_trees=True and 600 estimators, using the same seed.

Append out-of-fold nearest-positive and nearest-negative ECFP4 Tanimoto similarity features (max positive similarity, max negative similarity, and their difference) to the LightGBM inputs, with training rows scored against other scaffold-grouped folds.

Append a 64-component TruncatedSVD embedding (fit without labels on the count Morgan fingerprints of train plus test molecules, random_state=seed) to the LightGBM feature matrix, keeping all other settings unchanged.
Abort: RDKit 2D descriptors are already in the current train.py, so this idea would be a duplicate.
Abort the ionization-state SMARTS idea: the current featurize() already appends every RDKit 2D descriptor, which covers most of the proposed counts.

Switch the LightGBM predictor to DART boosting (drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, max_drop=50, learning_rate=0.1, 300 estimators) as a dropout-style regularizer, leaving featurize() and the rest of the script unchanged.

Aborted the logistic-regression idea: it swaps the LightGBM predictor for a linear model on descriptors, which is a model-family swap that the experiment notes say to avoid and that earlier comparable swaps (CatBoost, SVM, ExtraTrees, XGBoost) were aborted or rejected for.

issues: No integrity problems. The diff has no file or network access and no pasted answers. Test labels are never used: test_smiles is only featurized and passed to predict_proba. All randomness comes from seed+k.

No bugs that would make the result meaningless. Each of the 6 LightGBM models uses the same column subset for training and for prediction. The returned output is the averaged class-1 probability, one value per test molecule.

Recomputed z = (0.0962 - 0.0932) / (0.0049 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/1)) = 0.0030 / 0.00693 ≈ 0.43. This matches the reported 0.434. The candidate scores 0.0030 better, which is well inside the noise of one run per side, so the provisional reject is consistent with the numbers.

Minor point: the candidate fits 6 times as many models per fold, so its job will take noticeably longer. It should still stay under the 10-minute limit, but this extra cost matters given the 'simpler is better' rule, because the gain is not significant. If the idea is worth pursuing, a replicate run would be needed before accepting it.

description: Replace the single LightGBM fit with an equal-weight average of 6 LightGBM models, each trained on all rows and a different random 50% of the feature columns (RandomState(seed + k)), with colsample_bytree set to 1.0.

Replace the 31-leaf LightGBM settings with a shallow, strongly regularised regime (num_leaves=7, max_depth=3, 1200 trees at learning rate 0.03, min_child_samples=30, reg_lambda=5.0, reg_alpha=0.5, colsample 0.2, subsample 0.7, min_split_gain=0.01), leaving the feature set and seed handling unchanged.
Append smoothed out-of-fold target encoding of fused ring-system strings (m=10, 5 inner folds) plus the ring-system count as two extra LightGBM features, leaving existing features unchanged.

Append presence/absence columns for up to 512 BRICS fragments (vocabulary built inside fit_predict from training molecules only, fragments in at least 5 training molecules) to the existing Morgan count and descriptor matrix.

Two-stage gain-based feature pruning: fit the current LightGBM on all features, keep the 300 columns with the highest total split gain (training data only), and refit the same LightGBM settings on those columns for prediction.

Append the 315-dimensional ErG pharmacophore reduced-graph fingerprint (rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint, zero-vector fallback on failure) as an extra dense block in featurize(), with LightGBM settings unchanged.

Append a parameter-free graph-propagated atom feature block (per-atom element one-hot, degree, charge, aromaticity, H count, ring membership, averaged over self-looped neighbours for 4 hops, sum and mean pooled) to the existing Morgan-count and descriptor features, leaving the LightGBM model unchanged.

Average the LightGBM predictions from four boosting snapshots (num_iteration 100, 200, 300, 400) with equal weight instead of using only the final 400-round model, with no change to featurize() or the LightGBM settings.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only changes LightGBM settings: 800 trees, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 20, and a learning rate that falls linearly from 0.1 to 0.01 through the reset_parameter callback. It adds no file or network access, no pasted answers and no use of test labels. The seed is still passed to random_state.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The schedule list has 800 entries, which matches n_estimators=800, so reset_parameter will not run out of values. predict_proba[:, 1] still returns the probability of class 1.

Recomputed z from the rounded numbers: (0.0962 - 0.1011) / (0.0049 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/1)) = -0.0049 / 0.00693 = -0.707. This is close to the reported -0.699; the gap is likely from rounding of the shown values. Both runs are single runs, so the result is weak evidence. The candidate is worse by about one noise sd, so the provisional reject is consistent with the numbers.
Minor: the diff also fixes the incumbent's misaligned continuation indent. This changes nothing.

description: Train the LightGBM predictor with a linearly decaying learning rate (0.1 to 0.01 over 800 rounds) via reset_parameter, with num_leaves=15 and min_child_samples=20, keeping the same feature and bagging fractions.

Append one transductive label-spreading score (ECFP4 Tanimoto 10-NN graph over train+test, 0.8 propagation, 30 iterations, out-of-fold for training rows) as an extra LightGBM feature, with the class-1 score normalised by the total spread mass.
Add LightGBM monotone constraints: -1 on TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, MolWt, NumRotatableBonds, +1 on MolLogP, 0 on all Morgan count columns, using method='advanced'.
Append a 1000-column bag of SMILES character 2-6-gram counts (CountVectorizer fitted on training SMILES only, min_df=5) to the existing featurize() matrix before the unchanged LightGBM fit.

After the LightGBM predicts test probabilities, smooth each one over the test-test Morgan radius-2 Tanimoto graph (top 5 neighbours with similarity above 0.4, 0.5 own + 0.5 neighbour mean, unchanged if no neighbour qualifies), clipped to [0,1], using test inputs only.
Replace the LightGBM predictor with Tanimoto-kernel ridge regression on count Morgan vectors, using a lambda grid searched by an inner scaffold-grouped split.
Abort the tuned RandomForest idea: train.py no longer contains a RandomForest (it was replaced by LightGBM in slot 0), so the requested max_features/min_samples_leaf change has no target.

Replace the hashed 2048-bit Morgan count vector with an unfolded Morgan vocabulary built from training molecules only (IDs seen in at least 5 training molecules), keeping the RDKit descriptors and LightGBM settings unchanged.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted answers, no use of test labels. The new ring and shape features (ring-system count and size, aromatic and aliphatic ring counts, Fsp3, stereocentre count, rotatable bonds, heavy atoms per ring atom) are computed from each molecule's own structure only, so nothing leaks across folds.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The loop that merges rings into ring systems is correct: rings that share atoms end up in one system. The default values handle molecules with no rings. Like the incumbent, the code assumes every SMILES parses, so this adds no new crash risk.

Recomputed z = (0.0962 - 0.0943) / (0.0049 * sqrt(2)) ≈ 0.274, using one run per side. That matches the reported 0.276 within rounding of the inputs. The gain of 0.0019 is about 0.4 of one run's noise sd, so 'reject' is consistent with the numbers. Only one run was done for each script, so if the budget allows, a replicate run could confirm or rule out a small real gain.
Minor: the ring_features helper adds about 25 lines for a gain that is not yet significant. By the 'simpler is better' rule, it should not be adopted unless a replicate confirms the gain.

description: Append eight ring-topology features (ring-system count, largest ring system size, aromatic and non-aromatic ring counts, Fsp3, stereocentre count, rotatable bonds, heavy-to-ring-atom ratio) to the existing LightGBM feature matrix, leaving the model unchanged.

Append six Gasteiger partial-charge statistics (max, min, sum of absolute charges, sum of positive charges, sum of negative charges, and the charge of the most polar N/O atom) to the existing Morgan count and RDKit descriptor features.

Abort: the auxiliary targets TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP and NumHDonors are already exact columns in the current feature matrix (Descriptors.descList), so the stacked regressors could only add lossy reconstructions of inputs the classifier already sees.
Append RDKit's 192-value 2D autocorrelation descriptor vector (CalcAUTOCORR2D, NaN replaced by 0) to each molecule's feature row in featurize(), leaving the LightGBM settings unchanged.
Per-atom Crippen contribution histograms
MQN and EState count descriptors appended
Distilling out-of-fold random-forest probabilities as soft targets
Out-of-fold smoothed log-odds encoding of Morgan bits
Stump-based additive boosting (EBM-style GAM)
Append RDKit path-based and Avalon fingerprints
Path-smoothed leaf values as a regulariser
Inverse-density sample weights from Tanimoto neighbourhoods
